ethics_check.title: Ethics Approval Check
ethics_check.summary_text: All papers that appeared to involve live data collection contained an ethics approval statement.

table.text: Ethical approval was provided by the Wales Research Ethics Committee 3 (25/WA/0047).
Clinicians were recruited through social media and professional networks, and patients/carers through a third-sector organisation.

Lived experience participants were aged 18 years or older with current or lifetime history of self-harm and experience of attending general practice services, or experience of caring for someone with these experiences.
Participants were also required to understand written and verbal English and have capacity to provide informed consent.
Two focus groups were recruited for patients/carers, and two focus groups were recruited for clinicians.
Seven to eight participants were recruited for each focus group.

Our sample size was based on ensuring data adequacy and information richness and was guided by previous research findings on this topic. (23) (24) (25) Staff were recruited through social media and professional networks covering the North West and Midlands NHS regions in England.
table.formatted: Our sample size was based on ensuring data adequacy and information richness and was guided by previous research findings on this topic. <ref type="bibr" target="#b22">(23)</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b23">(24)</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b24">(25)</ref> Staff were recruited through social media and professional networks covering the North West and Midlands NHS regions in England.

table.text: Patients/carers were recruited purposively through collaboration with a UK-based third-sector organisation for people affected by self-harm.
As a token of appreciation, participants were given shopping vouchers (£25 per hour of data collection) and participation certificates.
Participants were encouraged to raise suggestions or requirements for a knowledge support tool outside of those presented within the topic guide.

Participants were asked semi-structured questions around the acceptability and implementation of the tool, during which they were prompted to further consider its content and functionality requirements.

Characteristics of focus group participants are reported in 258 Table 1 and additional characteristics relating to clinician job roles are in Table 2 1 One participant reported working both on a part-time and voluntary basis.

ethics_check.report:
Based on the following text, we would expect an ethics approval statement, and it was present:

> Clinicians were recruited through social media and professional networks, and patients/carers through a third-sector organisation.

> Lived experience participants were aged 18 years or older with current or lifetime history of self-harm and experience of attending general practice services, or experience of caring for someone with these experiences.

> Participants were also required to understand written and verbal English and have capacity to provide informed consent.

> Two focus groups were recruited for patients/carers, and two focus groups were recruited for clinicians.

> Seven to eight participants were recruited for each focus group.

> Our sample size was based on ensuring data adequacy and information richness and was guided by previous research findings on this topic. (23) (24) (25) Staff were recruited through social media and professional networks covering the North West and Midlands NHS regions in England.

> Patients/carers were recruited purposively through collaboration with a UK-based third-sector organisation for people affected by self-harm.

> As a token of appreciation, participants were given shopping vouchers (£25 per hour of data collection) and participation certificates.

> Participants were encouraged to raise suggestions or requirements for a knowledge support tool outside of those presented within the topic guide.

> Participants were asked semi-structured questions around the acceptability and implementation of the tool, during which they were prompted to further consider its content and functionality requirements.

> Characteristics of focus group participants are reported in 258 Table 1 and additional characteristics relating to clinician job roles are in Table 2 1 One participant reported working both on a part-time and voluntary basis.

> Quantitative ratings of perceived utility for suggested content and 268 functionality of the knowledge support tool 269 Participants provided utility ratings for suggested content and functionality of a 270 knowledge support tool (Figure 1) and illustrative examples (Supplementary Table S7).

> Additionally, patient/carer participants were predominantly female.

Ethics approval statement:

> Ethical approval was provided by the Wales Research Ethics Committee 3 (25/WA/0047).

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::
